registers.name: CONTROL
registers.description: Control register. Bit 0 enables controller operation, bit 1 requests a software soft reset action, and bit 2 enables interrupt generation.

fields.name: ENABLE
fields.description: When set, enables normal controller operation and memory access sequencing.

fields.name: SOFT_RESET
fields.description: Software-visible reset request. Clears controller-visible status and control state when serviced.

fields.name: IRQ_ENABLE
fields.description: When set, allows irq assertion on latched BIST completion or failure events.

registers.name: STATUS
registers.description: Status register reporting controller readiness and BIST outcome state.

fields.name: ready
fields.description: Controller ready indication.

fields.name: bist_done
fields.description: Latched BIST completion status.

fields.name: bist_fail
fields.description: Latched BIST failure status.

fields.name: busy
fields.description: Indicates the controller is actively servicing a memory or BIST-related operation.

registers.name: MEM_ADDR
registers.description: Scratchpad memory address register. Only bits [7:0] are used.

fields.name: memory_address
fields.description: 8-bit word address for the 256x32 scratchpad memory.

fields.name: memory_write_data
fields.description: 32-bit data written into the scratchpad memory on a write request.

fields.name: memory_read_data
fields.description: Most recently captured read data from the scratchpad memory.

registers.name: MEM_CONTROL
registers.description: Memory access control register. Requests are one-shot semantics and should be interpreted by firmware as a simple command interface.

fields.name: MEM_WRITE
fields.description: Request a memory write using MEM_ADDR and MEM_WDATA.

fields.name: MEM_READ
fields.description: Request a memory read using MEM_ADDR; read data is captured into MEM_RDATA.

fields.name: START
fields.description: Software request to start a BIST operation, functionally equivalent to asserting bist_start.

fields.name: CLEAR_RESULT
fields.description: Clears latched BIST result and related interrupt status.

registers.name: BIST_STATUS
registers.description: BIST status register reporting result latch state and the last observed failure address.

fields.name: done
fields.description: BIST done latch.

fields.name: fail
fields.description: BIST fail latch.

fields.name: running
fields.description: Indicates a BIST request is active or being serviced.

fields.name: last_fail_addr
fields.description: Last failing memory address, if any, in bits [7:0].

registers.name: IRQ_STATUS
registers.description: Interrupt status register. Bits latch BIST events until cleared by software.

fields.name: bist_done
fields.description: Latched BIST done interrupt status. Write 1 to clear.

fields.name: bist_fail
fields.description: Latched BIST fail interrupt status. Write 1 to clear.

registers.name: IRQ_CLEAR
registers.description: Write-one-to-clear helper for IRQ status. Writing a 1 clears the corresponding IRQ_STATUS bits.

fields.name: clear
fields.description: Write 1 to clear latched IRQ status bits.

sources.name: BIST_DONE_IRQ
sources.description: Asserts when BIST completion is latched in IRQ_STATUS and IRQ_ENABLE is set.

sources.name: BIST_FAIL_IRQ
sources.description: Asserts when BIST failure is latched in IRQ_STATUS and IRQ_ENABLE is set.

init_sequence: Assert reset and wait for controller reset completion.
Write CONTROL with ENABLE=1 and IRQ_ENABLE as required by firmware policy.
Program MEM_ADDR with the target scratchpad word address.
Program MEM_WDATA before a write operation.
Issue a memory write by writing MEM_CONTROL.MEM_WRITE=1, then clear the request bit if the implementation expects edge-pulsed software commands.
Issue a memory read by writing MEM_CONTROL.MEM_READ=1, then poll MEM_RDATA or rd_data for the returned value.
If BIST is desired, write BIST_CONTROL.START=1 or assert the top-level bist_start input.
If needed, clear latched BIST results by writing BIST_CONTROL.CLEAR_RESULT=1 or using IRQ_CLEAR / RW1C behavior on IRQ_STATUS.
polling_sequence: Poll STATUS.ready to confirm the controller is available.
Poll STATUS.busy to determine whether a memory or BIST request is still being serviced.
Poll BIST_STATUS.done and BIST_STATUS.fail to determine BIST outcome.
Read BIST_STATUS.last_fail_addr to identify the failing address when fail is asserted.
Read MEM_RDATA after a memory read request to capture the returned scratchpad data.
irq_sequence: Issue BIST via bist_start or BIST_CONTROL.START.
Read IRQ_STATUS to determine whether the event was done or fail.
Clear the interrupt source by writing 1s to IRQ_CLEAR or using the RW1C behavior on IRQ_STATUS.
Optionally clear BIST_STATUS via BIST_CONTROL.CLEAR_RESULT before the next test cycle.

consistency_notes: All assumptions remain compatible with DIGITAL_SPEC_JSON.
The register map preserves the specified register names, addresses, access types, and field semantics.
No new hierarchy, ports, or bus protocol are introduced.
The register interface is described as abstract because the top-level RTL contract provides local read/write strobes rather than an external standardized bus.
